title: Photo of a cement building band; Mr. Chaplin and Tony Dianapolis
summary: Sal talks about a violinist, an old club owner, and Joe Capra on banjo.

story.theme_name: Chicago: the jazz migration and its clubs
story.community_name: Going north: working the Chicago jazz scene

blocks.x: I wanted to ask you, these guys look familiar in this picture here. Looks like you're playing in some sort of a cement block building. Right, right, right, right.
You know that Night Man, I got in the record?

Yeah. You know, one of them. It was down in Baraka. And this guy here, Mr. Chaplin, the little violin player, he played, Jesus, before my time. He talked about the Fantan and the Chinggadilly, Jesus Christ. Back, way back when, man. One time, he used to tie your horse and bike into the horse and wear the street, you know, the little things that don't work. You seen him, you know that? You know, stand there. I worked over there, man, I said, Santa Suey, see, man. With George Traai. Right way back, man. I talked to him on the phone. He has a beautiful hand right there, he waits for Jimmy Comiskin, that's his office. One time, Mr. Penman said, he's made beautiful, in the books, you know.

The only guy who plays violin, they don't play corny. And good tempo, man. He likes all the tunes that I like, man. This man had the first Walsh record in the city of New Orleans, Walsh automobile, on the Island Broad, and he was Chaps. Man, big diamond ring, he was a good friend of the guy, they owned a little club, Tony Dianapolis. And Mike had the Hatsitatsi. And Joe Capra was playing banjo up there. Joe and the Happy Bruns, and Holly Shalane. Oh, man. And I played the TMA club, man. With Jack Lapine, man. Boy, you know.
